title: Per-account locking for ledger journal posting
name: Ledger journal posting

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code acquires and releases account locks? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why does post() acquire account locks in sorted id order?
choices: So the store's append writes postings in id order
Because Map iteration requires sorted keys
To speed up lookups in the lock table
So two concurrent journals touching overlapping accounts always lock in the same order and cannot wait on each other in a cycle

questions.prompt: A journal debits account A by 500 and credits A by 300 and B by 200, and A's balance is 250 with no overdraft. What does the funds check do?
choices: Rejects, because the 500 debit alone exceeds the balance
Accepts, because A's net change is -200 and 250 - 200 >= 0
Rejects, because B has a positive delta
Skips the check entirely because the journal balances

questions.prompt: store.balance throws a network error while post() holds locks on two accounts. What happens to those locks?
choices: They are released in the finally block, in reverse acquisition order
They remain held until the AccountLockTable is garbage-collected
Only the most recently acquired lock is released
They are released only if the error is an InsufficientFundsError
